goal: Turn Docket from a tool that schedules posts someone else wrote into one that can run a brand's content backlog on its own: hold the brand's identity as data, generate its own images, keep standing and date-pegged content series producing posts without anyone re-creating a job each week, and expose project setup over the API so onboarding a brand stops being a manual pass through the UI.

entries.title: Hold a project's tagline, description and website as project data
entries.description: Today a brand's identity lives nowhere in Docket: `projects` (src/server/db/schema/projects.ts) has only name, slug, timezone, the two default policies and defaultVoiceProfileId. The website ends up smuggled into a voice profile's `preferredLinks` (src/lib/validation/voice.ts), and the tagline and description live outside the product entirely, so every generated post that wants to say what the product is depends on someone having repeated it inside a voice-profile free-text field. Add three nullable text columns to `projects` via a committed SQL migration (`pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm db:check` green): `tagline` (<=200 chars, the one-sentence description), `description` (<=1000 chars, the longer one) and `websiteUrl` (http/https only, validated like `preferredLinks` in src/lib/validation/voice.ts, <=500 chars). Surface them on the project settings form (src/app/p/[projectSlug]/settings/settings-form.tsx) with owner/admin-only writes enforced server-side (`project: ['edit']` via src/server/auth/access.ts), through the service in src/server/services/projects.ts, and audit each change in the project activity log the way posting-instruction edits already are. Feed them into generation: src/server/services/generation/prompt.ts should carry the tagline, description and website as explicit, labelled brand context ahead of the voice profile, so a generated post can state what the product is and link it without the voice profile having to repeat it; update the golden prompt tests (prompt.golden.test.ts, prompt.test.ts) and record in docs/decisions.md how brand context and voice profile are ordered and what happens when a field is empty. Keep `preferredLinks` on voice profiles working unchanged — a campaign link is not the same thing as the project's identity — and document the distinction in docs/generator.md. Tests: migration, validation (bad URL, over-length, empty-to-set-to-empty), authz for editor vs admin, audit rows, and prompt composition with every combination of set/unset. This entry does NOT add a logo or avatar field (media is post attachments; the brand avatar lives on each platform), does NOT add per-platform profile copy or any profile-sync to Facebook/Instagram/Threads/Bluesky, and does NOT expose these fields over the public API — `setup-write-api` owns that.
entries.rationale: First because it is the smallest change to the project model and everything after it reads the result: the image prompts in `image-generation` and the standing series in `evergreen-series` both want to know what the product is and where to send people, and `setup-write-api` should publish a project shape that has already settled. It depends on nothing new, and getting the brand-context-versus-voice-profile ordering decided once, with golden tests, avoids re-litigating it inside every later generation change.

entries.title: Generate images into the media library, behind the existing ImageGenerator extension point
entries.description: src/server/llm/image-generation.ts already declares the contract — `ImageGenerationRequest { projectId, prompt, aspect?, size? }`, `ImageGenerationResult`, `ImageGenerator` — and says in its own comment that it is an extension point only, with no implementation, configuration or UI. Implement it. Add an image-capable provider alongside the text providers in src/server/llm (openai.ts, anthropic.ts, config.ts, types.ts), following the same resolution and credential pattern config.ts already uses, including the per-project credential work from 065-per-project-llm and the credit-hold behaviour in src/server/services/generation/credit.ts and src/server/db/schema/generation.ts (`llm_credit_holds`) — a billing refusal from the image provider must take the same hold path as a text refusal, not fail loudly per request. Start with OpenAI's image model since the `openai` dependency and credentials already exist, but keep the model id out of source (there is a `no-model-literal.test.ts` guarding exactly this) and make the provider swappable, because text rendering inside generated images is the weak point for sports graphics and the best provider for that will change. A generated image must land in the media library as a normal asset: write through src/server/services/media.ts into `mediaAssets` (src/server/db/schema/media.ts, `kind = 'image'`) and S3 via src/server/storage, so variants (src/server/services/media-variants.ts), fit checks (media-fit.ts) and every existing per-platform constraint in src/providers/media.ts apply unchanged; record provenance on the asset (that it was generated, with the prompt and provider/model) via a committed migration, and never store credentials in it. Requires media storage: when storage is not configured, fail with the same 'Media storage is not set up.' message src/server/llm/images.ts already uses, and hide the UI. UI: an owner/admin-visible 'Generate an image' action on the Media page (src/app/p/[projectSlug]/media/page.tsx) taking a prompt and an aspect, showing the generated asset in the library on success; follow the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md, announce the outcome through a LiveRegion, label every control, full keyboard use. Tests: provider mapping and error shapes, credit-hold on billing refusal, storage-not-configured, asset + variant creation, prompt/provenance persistence, project isolation, authz, and the secret-scan test. Update docs/storage.md and docs/generator.md, and log judgement calls in docs/decisions.md. This entry does NOT wire image generation into the post generator or into jobs — a post that needs an image still gets one from the library, and `evergreen-series` is what makes a series produce its own; it does NOT generate images of real people (record that as a decision: likeness and publicity rights make athlete portraits a legal problem, and the project's own voice profiles already forbid using a real child's likeness), and it does NOT add video generation.
entries.rationale: Second because it removes the one hard blocker on a whole channel: every Instagram post requires media, so with an empty library the Instagram account cannot publish at all, no matter how good the text generation is. It is also self-contained — it implements an interface that already exists on main, writes through the media service that already exists, and changes no posting or scheduling behaviour — so it can be reviewed on its own merits before anything depends on it. It must land before `evergreen-series`, because a standing Instagram series is pointless if each run still needs a human to supply a picture.

entries.title: Standing content series that keep producing posts on a cadence
entries.description: Generation jobs today are finite: src/server/services/jobs/create.ts builds a job from a fixed source (sources/csv.ts, sources/media.ts, sources/api.ts), the runner (runner.ts) works through its items, and manage.ts closes it. A content backlog needs the opposite — a standing series that keeps emitting posts on a cadence until someone stops it. Add a recurring series: a new table (committed migration) holding projectId, name, the voiceProfileId and `template`/`templateFields` shape that `generation_jobs` already uses (src/server/db/schema/jobs.ts), the target accounts, a cadence (how many posts per period, which period), the approval and scheduling policy to apply, an enabled flag, and `lastRunAt`/`nextRunAt`. A worker pass — in the existing scheduler/worker loop (src/worker.ts, src/server/scheduler) rather than a new process — wakes due series, generates the period's posts through the existing generation path (src/server/services/generation/core.ts and series.ts, so prompts, schema validation, failures in generation/failures.ts and the credit hold all behave exactly as a manual Generate does), and applies the project's approval and scheduling policy through src/server/services/generation/policy.ts — meaning a validation failure still forces review even under auto-approve, which is intended behaviour and must not be routed around. Posts that are set to queue use the existing allocator so they land in the account's real posting slots and never double-book. Where a target account requires media (Instagram, TikTok — see src/providers and docs/limits.md), the series either draws from a configured media pool or, when the project has image generation configured, generates one per post through the `ImageGenerator` implemented in `image-generation`; a series that cannot satisfy its media requirement records the reason and skips that post rather than emitting an invalid one. Idempotency and concurrency are part of this entry: a series must not double-generate when two worker ticks overlap or the process restarts mid-run (claim the due series the way jobs/claims.ts claims work), and must be bounded per tick. UI: a Series section under the existing Batch jobs area (src/app/p/[projectSlug]/jobs) to create, pause, resume and delete a series and see its recent runs and failures; owner/admin only for create/edit, enforced server-side; follow the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md. Tests: integration tests for cadence firing and not firing, restart and overlapping-tick idempotency, policy application (auto-approve vs review, queue vs draft), no slot double-booking across concurrent series, media-required skip, generation failure handling, credit hold pausing a series cleanly, project isolation and authz. Update docs/generator.md and docs/decisions.md. This entry does NOT add date-pegged occurrences — `dated-series` builds that on the cadence engine defined here — and does NOT change one-off Generate or the existing finite batch jobs beyond shared refactoring.
entries.rationale: Third because it is the feature that turns a content plan into infrastructure, and it is the one with the most new behaviour to settle: cadence firing, idempotency across worker restarts, and how a standing series interacts with approval policy and slot allocation. It needs `image-generation` in place so a media-required channel is a first-class case rather than a later retrofit, and it needs the brand context from `brand-profile-fields` so standing posts can say what the product is. It must land before `dated-series`, which is a second occurrence rule on the same engine — building the engine once, with its concurrency story reviewed, is much cheaper than bolting recurrence onto a date-driven special case.

entries.title: Date-pegged series: content that fires on an anniversary, from a spreadsheet
entries.description: Add a second occurrence rule to the series engine from `evergreen-series`: instead of 'n posts per period', a series can be driven by a dated list — each row carrying a month/day (optionally a year), the fields the template needs, and an optional media reference. This is how a brand runs birthdays, anniversaries and 'on this day' content without anyone writing them weekly: upload once, and the series fires each row on its date, every year unless the row names a year. Reuse the CSV ingestion that already exists for jobs (src/server/services/jobs/sources/csv.ts and its tests) rather than inventing a second parser, extended with a validated date column; rows with unparseable or impossible dates are reported on import and skipped, not silently dropped. Store rows in a table keyed to the series (committed migration), editable and re-importable. The worker pass resolves 'which rows are due' in the project's time zone (src/server/db/schema/projects.ts `timezone`, via the Temporal usage the codebase already standardises on), and must handle the cases that make date recurrence bite: Feb 29 in a non-leap year (record the chosen rule in docs/decisions.md), a row whose date passes while the series is paused or the worker is down (fire late within a bounded window, or skip — decide and document), two rows on the same date, a lead time so a post can be generated and reviewed before the date rather than on it, and the same restart/overlap idempotency as the cadence rule so a row never fires twice. Generated posts go through the identical generation, policy and allocation path as `evergreen-series` — no separate code path. UI: on the series screen, importing and viewing a dated list, showing the next few upcoming rows and any rows that failed to import; owner/admin only, server-enforced; follow the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md. Tests: import validation and error reporting, due-date resolution across time zones and DST, leap day, missed-window behaviour, lead time, duplicate dates, idempotency across restarts and overlapping ticks, project isolation and authz. Update docs/generator.md and docs/decisions.md. This entry does NOT fetch dates from any external source or API, does NOT generate images of real people (the constraint recorded in `image-generation` holds — a dated series about a public figure is text and typography, not a likeness), and does NOT change the cadence rule's semantics.
entries.rationale: Fourth because it is a second occurrence rule on an engine that `evergreen-series` has already settled: with cadence firing, idempotency, policy application and slot allocation reviewed and in place, this entry is mostly date arithmetic and an importer. Doing it after also means the genuinely fiddly parts — leap days, missed windows, lead time, time-zone resolution — get decided against a working engine instead of being tangled up with inventing one. It reuses the existing CSV source rather than adding a parser, so it stays small.

entries.title: Public API for project setup: projects, voice profiles, posting instructions and slots
entries.description: The v1 API (src/app/api/v1/[[...path]], operations in src/server/api/operations/) is post-centric: it can list accounts and create posts, media and jobs, but there is no endpoint that creates a project, a voice profile or a posting slot, or sets an account's posting instructions. Every step of standing a brand up is therefore a manual pass through the browser. Add write operations, each calling exactly one existing service function: `POST /projects` (src/server/services/projects.ts — name, slug, timezone, the policy defaults and the brand fields from `brand-profile-fields`), `POST /voice-profiles` and `PATCH /voice-profiles/{id}` (src/server/services/voice.ts, validated by src/lib/validation/voice.ts, honouring the immutable-version model in `voice_profile_versions`), `PATCH /accounts/{accountId}` for posting instructions only (src/server/services/accounts.ts, the 2,000-character field, audited exactly as the UI edit is), and slot operations `POST /slots`, `PATCH /slots/{id}`, `DELETE /slots/{id}` (src/server/services/slots.ts) — including the whole-week add that 066-book-week-slots introduced, so the API can express the same intent as the grid rather than a weaker version of it. Each operation declares `resourceParams` for the cross-project scope test, is `idempotent: true` where a repeat should not duplicate (Idempotency-Key, research D8), and maps service errors to the existing API error shapes (slug already taken, bad timezone, over-length instructions, unknown account) rather than 500s. Request and response schemas go in src/lib/api/schemas.ts so the generated OpenAPI document (src/server/api/openapi.ts, operations/openapi.ts) describes them with examples, and the existing OpenAPI document test must stay green. Permissions: these are owner/admin-level operations, so decide whether the existing API-key permissions suffice or a new `api_key_permission` value is needed, and record the choice in docs/decisions.md; attribution must follow whatever actor model the audit log uses for API keys. Note the constraint worth documenting: `projects.slug` carries a global unique constraint across the whole install, so `POST /projects` must return a clean, non-leaking conflict when a slug is held by a project the caller cannot see. Tests: API integration tests per operation — happy path, validation failures, cross-project key, missing permission, idempotent replay, slug conflict — plus the OpenAPI document test and the secret-scan test. Update docs/n8n.md with a worked example that provisions a project end to end, and log decisions in docs/decisions.md. This entry does NOT add endpoints for connecting a social account (OAuth and app passwords are interactive and stay in the browser), does NOT add series endpoints, and does NOT change any existing endpoint's contract.
entries.rationale: Fifth because it publishes a contract, and a public contract is the costliest thing to change later: it should describe a project shape that `brand-profile-fields` has already added to and a slot API that includes the whole-week add from 066, rather than being extended twice. It depends on no new behaviour — every operation is a thin adapter over a service function that already exists — which is exactly why it should come after the behaviour changes rather than racing them.

entries.title: An MCP server over the v1 API
entries.description: Expose Docket to LLM clients through MCP, as a thin translation layer over the v1 API rather than a second implementation. The project already publishes an OpenAPI document (src/server/api/openapi.ts, src/server/api/operations/openapi.ts, built with zod-openapi) and already authenticates with API keys, so the tool surface should be derived from the operations table in src/server/api/operations/ rather than hand-maintained in parallel — a new operation should appear as a tool without a second edit, and a drift test should fail if the two ever diverge. Scope the exposed tools deliberately: reading posts, accounts and activity, composing and scheduling posts, and the setup operations from `setup-write-api`; keep destructive and irreversible operations either out or behind an explicit confirmation argument, and document which is which. Authentication uses an existing project-scoped API key with its existing permissions — no new credential type, no ambient access, and no operation reachable over MCP that the same key could not perform over HTTP. Tool descriptions matter more here than in a REST client, since a model picks tools from them: each needs the project scoping, the required permission and the failure modes stated plainly. Decide and record in docs/decisions.md how the server is hosted (a route in the Next app versus a separate process), and how the user's project is selected per session. Tests: tool-surface-matches-operations drift test, authentication and permission enforcement per tool, project isolation, and the secret-scan test. Document it in docs/ alongside docs/n8n.md so the API and MCP routes are presented as the two front doors onto the same operations. This entry does NOT add any capability that the v1 API lacks — if something is worth doing over MCP and has no endpoint, it belongs in an API entry first — and does NOT introduce a separate permission model.
entries.rationale: Last, and deliberately optional, because it is a translation layer with no behaviour of its own: its value is entirely a function of how much the v1 API can do, which is why `setup-write-api` has to land first. Built before that, an MCP server would expose the same post-centric surface the REST API already exposes and would not make onboarding a brand any less manual. Built after, it is close to free — generated from an OpenAPI document that already exists — and it is the piece that makes driving Docket conversationally worthwhile.
